items.text: משנת הפתיחה: דרכי קניין האישה והיבמה
items.text_en: Opening Mishnah
items.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a woman is acquired in three ways (money, document, intercourse) and acquires herself in two ways (divorce, husband's death). It then adds that a yevamah is acquired through intercourse and acquires herself through halitzah or the yavam's death.
items.desc: המשנה פותחת בקביעה שאישה נקנית לנישואין בשלוש דרכים: כסף, שטר וביאה, ומפרטת את שיעורי הכסף לפי בית שמאי ובית הלל. עוד היא קובעת שהאישה קונה את עצמה בגט או במיתת הבעל, והיבמה נקנית בביאה וקונה את עצמה בחליצה או במיתת היבם.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah opens by stating that a woman is acquired in three ways (money, document, intercourse) and specifies the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding the minimum amount of money.
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בקביעת דרכי הקניין וההיתר של האישה והיבמה, תוך מחלוקת בית שמאי ובית הלל בשיעור הכסף.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah defines the value of a פרוטה (perutah) as one-eighth of an Italian איסר (issar).
sub.desc: המשנה פותחת בקביעת דרכי הקניין וההיתר של האישה והיבמה, תוך מחלוקת בית שמאי ובית הלל בשיעור הכסף.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that a woman acquires herself (is freed from marriage) through a גט (bill of divorce) or the husband's death.
The Mishnah adds that a יבמה (yevamah, a widow awaiting levirate marriage) is acquired through intercourse and acquires herself through חליצה (halitzah) or the yavam's death.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא על לשון המשנה
items.text_en: Gemara's question on Mishnah's phrasing
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah uses the passive 'the woman is acquired' (נִקְנֵית) rather than the active 'the man betroths' (מְקַדֵּשׁ) as in other tractates. It answers that the Mishnah wants to teach about money, which leads to a derivation.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת מדוע המשנה תנאית 'האישה נקנית' בלשון נקבה, בעוד שבמקומות אחרים תנאית 'האיש מקדש' בלשון זכר. התשובה הראשונית היא משום שהמשנה רוצה להמשיך ולדון בכסף.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah here uses the passive 'the woman is acquired' (נִקְנֵית) while in other tractates it uses the active 'the man betroths' (מְקַדֵּשׁ).
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על השינוי בלשון המשנה: מדוע כאן נאמר 'האישה נקנית' בלשון נקבה, ואילו במסכת קידושין אחרת נאמר 'האיש מקדש' בלשון זכר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the Mishnah uses the passive because it wants to teach about the acquisition by money (כֶּסֶף), which leads to a derivation from Scripture.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על השינוי בלשון המשנה: מדוע כאן נאמר 'האישה נקנית' בלשון נקבה, ואילו במסכת קידושין אחרת נאמר 'האיש מקדש' בלשון זכר.

items.text: מקור הקניין בכסף מגזירה שווה
items.text_en: Derivation of money acquisition from verbal analogy
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks where the money acquisition is derived from, and answers via a verbal analogy (גזירה שווה) of the word 'taking' (קיחה) used both in 'when a man takes a woman' and in the field of Ephron ('take from me'). It then notes that 'taking' is called 'acquisition' (קניין), as in 'the field which Abraham acquired'.
items.desc: הגמרא מבארת את מקור הקניין בכסף מגזירה שווה של 'קיחה' 'קיחה' משדה עפרון: נאמר 'כי יקח איש אשה' ונאמר בשדה עפרון 'נתתי כסף השדה קח ממני', ומכאן שקניין כסף נקרא 'קניין'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks from where the money acquisition for betrothal is derived.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן נלמד שהכסף הוא אמצעי קניין לאשה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers via a גזירה שווה (verbal analogy) of the word 'taking' (קיחה) used both in the verse 'when a man takes a woman' and in the field of Ephron.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת מהיכן נלמד שהכסף הוא אמצעי קניין לאשה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara notes that 'taking' is called 'acquisition' (קניין), as in the verse 'the field which Abraham acquired'.

items.text: Defense of the Mishnah's passive formulation
items.text_en: Defense of the Mishnah's passive formulation
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah uses the passive 'a woman is acquired' rather than the active 'a man acquires'. It offers several answers: first, that the Mishnah initially uses biblical language and then rabbinic language; second, that the Mishnah wants to maintain consistency with the later clause about a woman acquiring herself; third, that the active form might imply coercion, which is not the case.

items.text: קושיית הגמרא על לשון 'שלוש'
items.text_en: Why 'three ways' and not 'three'
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah uses the feminine 'שלוש' (three) instead of the masculine 'שלושה', and answers that it is because the word 'דרך' (way) is feminine, as shown by a biblical verse.
items.desc: הגמרא מקשה מדוע המשנה תנת 'שלוש' (לשון נקבה) ולא 'שלושה' (לשון זכר), ומתרצת: משום שתנת 'דרך' שהוא לשון נקבה, כמו שכתוב 'והדרך ילכו בה'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah uses the feminine numeral 'שלש' instead of the masculine 'שלשה'.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מדוע המשנה תנת 'שלוש' בלשון נקבה ולא 'שלושה' בלשון זכר, ומתרצת: משום שתנת 'דרך' שהוא לשון נקבה, כמו שכתוב 'והדרך ילכו בה'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that 'דרך' is feminine, as shown by the verse 'את הדרך ילכו בה'.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה מדוע המשנה תנת 'שלוש' בלשון נקבה ולא 'שלושה' בלשון זכר, ומתרצת: משום שתנת 'דרך' שהוא לשון נקבה, כמו שכתוב 'והדרך ילכו בה'.

items.text: Resolving contradictions about the gender of 'דרך'
items.text_en: Resolving contradictions about the gender of 'דרך'
items.desc_en: The Gemara notes a contradiction: in another mishnah, 'seven ways' uses the masculine 'שבעה', not 'שבע'. It resolves this by explaining that the gender of 'דרך' depends on context: in Torah matters it is feminine, in war it is masculine. Similarly, in the context of a woman it is feminine, and in the context of a man (who is typically examined for זיבה) it is masculine.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises a contradiction: elsewhere the Mishnah says 'בשבעה דרכים' (masculine numeral) for examining a zav, and asks why it does not use the feminine 'שבע'.
The Gemara answers that 'דרך' can be masculine, as shown by the verse 'בדרך אחד יצאו אליך ובשבעה דרכים ינוסו לפניך'.

The Gemara resolves the contradiction: in Torah context 'דרך' is feminine, in war context masculine; similarly, the Mishnah uses feminine when discussing a woman (acquisition) and masculine when discussing a man (zav).

items.text: Why 'ways' and not 'things'
items.text_en: Why 'ways' and not 'things'
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah uses 'דרכים' (ways) instead of 'דברים' (things). It answers that the Mishnah intends to include 'ביאה' (sexual intercourse) as a mode of acquisition, and 'ביאה' is called a 'דרך' in Scripture. The other modes (money and document) are included because they are necessary for 'ביאה'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Mishnah uses 'דרכים' (ways) instead of 'דברים' (things), which would allow the masculine numeral 'שלשה'.
The Gemara answers that because the Mishnah includes 'ביאה' (sexual intercourse), which is called 'דרך' in the verse 'ודרך גבר בעלמה', it uses 'דרכים'.
The Gemara objects that this explanation works for 'ביאה' but not for 'כסף' and 'שטר', which are not called 'דרך'.
The Gemara answers that 'כסף' and 'שטר' are also necessary for 'ביאה', so the Mishnah uses 'דרכים' for all three.

items.text: תירוץ נוסף: רבי שמעון
items.text_en: Alternative answer: Rabbi Shimon's view
items.desc_en: The Gemara offers an alternative answer: the Mishnah follows Rabbi Shimon, who explains that the Torah uses the active 'a man takes a woman' because it is a man's way to pursue a woman, not vice versa. This supports the use of 'ways' in the Mishnah.
items.desc: הגמרא מציעה תירוץ אחר: המשנה כרבי שמעון, שאומר שדרך האיש לחזר על אשה, ולכן תנת בלשון נקבה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara offers an alternative answer: the Mishnah follows Rabbi Shimon, who explains that the Torah uses active language 'כי יקח איש אשה' because it is the man's way to pursue the woman, like a person seeking lost property.
sub.desc: הגמרא מציעה תירוץ נוסף: המשנה כרבי שמעון, הסובר שדרך האיש לחזר אחר האשה, ולכן לשון המשנה בלשון נקבה.

items.text: Other mishnayot using 'ways'
items.text_en: Other mishnayot using 'ways'
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains why other mishnayot also use 'דרכים' instead of 'דברים': in the case of the זב (one with a discharge), it teaches that certain ways (like excessive eating or drinking) lead to זיבה; in the case of the etrog, it is to maintain consistency with the later clause 'in one way'.

items.text: Clarification of 'דרכים' vs 'דברים'
items.text_en: Clarification of 'דרכים' vs 'דברים'
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah uses the term 'דרכים' (ways) instead of 'דברים' (matters), citing examples from other contexts where 'דברים' is used. It concludes that 'דרכים' is used where there is a dispute, as in the case of the etrog, while 'דברים' is used where there is no dispute, supported by the continuation of the Mishnah where Rabbi Eliezer offers a dissenting opinion.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Mishnah uses 'דרכים' (ways) instead of 'דברים' (matters), citing the etrog case and other examples where 'דברים' would be expected.
The Gemara answers that 'דרכים' is used where there is a dispute, as in the etrog case with Rabbi Eliezer's dissenting opinion, while 'דברים' is used where there is no dispute.

items.text: Question on the purpose of the numerical counts
items.text_en: Question on the purpose of the numerical counts
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the numerical counts at the beginning and end of the Mishnah's opening statement are meant to exclude, setting up the subsequent discussion.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what the numerical count at the beginning of the Mishnah excludes and what the numerical count at the end excludes.

items.text: Exclusion of חופה and חליפין
items.text_en: Exclusion of חופה and חליפין
items.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the first count excludes חופה (canopy) as a mode of acquisition, and for Rav Huna who derives חופה from a kal vachomer, it excludes חליפין (exchange). The Gemara explains that one might have thought to derive acquisition of a woman through חליפין from the field of Ephron, so the Mishnah teaches otherwise.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the first count excludes חופה (canopy) as a mode of acquisition, and for Rav Huna who derives חופה from a kal vachomer, it excludes חליפין (exchange).
The Gemara explains that one might have thought to derive acquisition of a woman through חליפין from the field of Ephron, so the Mishnah teaches otherwise.

items.text: Rejection of the exclusion of חליפין
items.text_en: Rejection of the exclusion of חליפין
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects that one might argue חליפין should be valid because it can be done with less than a perutah's worth, and a woman can be acquired with less than a perutah's worth, implying a potential parallel. The argument is cut off, indicating a continuation.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that one might argue חליפין (exchange) should be valid for acquiring a woman, since it can be done with less than a perutah's worth, and a woman can be acquired with less than a perutah's worth, implying a potential parallel.

items.text: Exclusion of Chalitzah from Kiddushin
items.text_en: Exclusion of Chalitzah from Kiddushin
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the second count of the Mishnah excludes chalitzah as a mode of acquisition for a woman. A kal vachomer from a yevamah would suggest otherwise, but the verse 'sefer keritut' teaches that only a get severs the marriage.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara states that the second count of the Mishnah excludes a mode of acquisition.
The Gemara asks what the second count excludes, and answers that it excludes חליצה (chalitzah).
The Gemara raises a possible קל וחומר (a fortiori argument) from a יבמה (yevamah) that would suggest chalitzah should also effect divorce here.
The Gemara states that the Mishnah teaches us otherwise, rejecting the kal vachomer.
The Gemara objects: why not say that chalitzah indeed works here?
The Gemara resolves by citing the verse 'ספר כריתת' (a bill of divorcement), teaching that only a גט (get) severs the marriage, not chalitzah.

items.text: Source for Acquisition by Money to Father
items.text_en: Source for Acquisition by Money to Father
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the source that a woman is acquired by money and that the money goes to her father. Rav Yehuda quoting Rav derives from the verse 'veyatz'ah chinam ein kesef' that there is money for another master, i.e., the father.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks for the source that a woman is acquired by money (בכסף) and that the money goes to her father.
Rav Yehuda citing Rav derives from the verse 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם אֵין כָּסֶף' that there is money for another master, i.e., the father.

items.text: Rejection of Daughter Receiving Money
items.text_en: Rejection of Daughter Receiving Money
items.desc_en: The Gemara rejects the possibility that the daughter herself receives the money, since her father accepts her kiddushin. For a na'arah who can accept her own kiddushin, the verse 'bin'ureha beit aviha' teaches that all the benefit of her youth belongs to her father.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: why not say the daughter herself receives the money, given that her father accepts her kiddushin?
The Gemara answers: the verse 'בִּנְעֻרֶיהָ בֵּית אָבִיהָ' teaches that all the benefit of her youth belongs to her father, even for a na'arah who can accept her own kiddushin.

items.text: Source for Daughter's Earnings to Father
items.text_en: Source for Daughter's Earnings to Father
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions Rav Huna's derivation that a daughter's earnings belong to her father from the verse about selling a daughter as a maidservant, since it could be derived from 'bin'ureha'. It explains that verse is about annulling vows, and one cannot learn monetary law from prohibitions, fines, or boshet and pegam.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions Rav Huna's derivation that a daughter's earnings belong to her father from the verse about selling a daughter as a maidservant, since it could be derived from 'bin'ureha'.
The Gemara explains that the verse 'bin'ureha' is about annulling vows, and one cannot learn monetary law from prohibitions.
The Gemara rejects the possibility of learning from fines (קנס), stating that monetary law cannot be derived from fines.
The Gemara rejects learning from boshet and pegam (indignity and depreciation), since the father is inherently involved in those cases.

items.text: Conclusion of the Derivation
items.text_en: Conclusion of the Derivation
items.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that the verse 'bin'ureha' is indeed used to exclude something else, implying that the father's right to earnings is derived from the maidservant verse.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that the verse 'bin'ureha' is indeed used to exclude something else, implying that the father's right to earnings is derived from the maidservant verse.

items.text: Gemara's objection to the derivation of 'yetziah'
items.text_en: Gemara's objection to the derivation of 'yetziah'
items.desc_en: The Gemara objects that the 'yetziah' (going out) of a maidservant is not comparable to that of a daughter, as the maidservant leaves the master's authority completely, while the daughter still requires transfer to the chuppah. However, it is relevant for the matter of annulling vows, as the father and betrothed jointly annul her vows.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that the 'yetziah' (going out) of a maidservant is not comparable to that of a daughter, as the maidservant leaves the master's authority completely, while the daughter still requires transfer to the chuppah.
The Gemara resolves that the comparison is relevant for the matter of annulling vows, as the father and betrothed jointly annul her vows.

items.text: Ravina's interpretation of 'ein kesef'
items.text_en: Ravina's interpretation of 'ein kesef'
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether the verse 'v'yatz'ah chinam' is needed for the earlier teaching about days of bagrut and na'arut. Ravina answers that the phrase 'ein kesef' implies there is no money for this master but there is money for another master, namely the father.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether the verse 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' (and she shall go out free) is needed only for the earlier teaching about days of bagrut and na'arut, since it already serves that purpose.
Ravina answers that the phrase 'אֵין כָּסֶף' (no money) implies there is no money for this master but there is money for another master, namely the father.

items.text: Derivation from 'v'zera ein lah'
items.text_en: Derivation from 'v'zera ein lah'
items.desc_en: The Gemara derives from the verse 'v'zera ein lah' that not only her own offspring but also her offspring's offspring and even unfit offspring are included. It then clarifies that the case of offspring's offspring is not needed, as grandchildren are like children, so the verse is only needed for unfit offspring.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: from where do we derive this interpretation? It cites a baraita that begins with the verse 'וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ'.
The baraita expounds: I only have her own offspring; offspring's offspring and unfit offspring are derived from the extra wording 'עַיֵּין לָהּ'.
The Gemara resolves: the case of offspring's offspring is unnecessary because grandchildren are like children, so the verse is only needed for unfit offspring.

items.text: Proof from the spelling of 'me'en'
items.text_en: Proof from the spelling of 'me'en'
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks how the Tanna himself derives this, and answers that the word 'me'en' is spelled with a yud here, unlike in the cases of Bilaam and yavam, indicating it is for exposition.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks how the Tanna himself derives the exposition of 'ויצאה חנם' (she goes free for nothing) from the spelling of 'אין כסף' (no money).

The Gemara answers that the word 'מאן' (refused) is spelled with a yud here ('מֵאֵן'), unlike in the cases of Bilaam and yavam where it is spelled without a yud, indicating that the word is meant for exposition.

items.text: Need for both verses: kiddushin and ma'aseh yadeha
items.text_en: Need for both verses: kiddushin and ma'aseh yadeha
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that both verses are necessary: one for her betrothal money and one for her handiwork. If only betrothal money were written, one might think it's because she didn't toil for it, but handiwork, which she toils for, would be hers. Conversely, if only handiwork were written, one might think it's because she is sustained from it, but betrothal money, which comes from elsewhere, would be hers.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara states that both verses are necessary: one for her betrothal money and one for her handiwork.
The Gemara explains that if only betrothal money were written, one might think it's because she didn't toil for it, but handiwork, which she toils for, would be hers.
The Gemara explains that if only handiwork were written, one might think it's because she is sustained from it, but betrothal money, which comes from elsewhere, would be hers.

items.text: Question on the need for both bagrut and na'arut
items.text_en: Question on the need for both bagrut and na'arut
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the verse mentions both bagrut and na'arut, since one could be derived from the other. Rabba answers that one teaches about the other.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions why the Torah wrote both bagrut (majority) and na'arut (minority) in the verse, since one could be derived from the other.
Rabba answers that the verse mentions both terms because one teaches about the other, i.e., bagrut teaches about na'arut or vice versa.

items.text: Analogy from toshav and sakhir
items.text_en: Analogy from toshav and sakhir
items.desc_en: The Gemara brings a baraita about a toshav (acquired for eternity) and a sakhir (acquired for years) to illustrate how one term can teach about another. If only 'toshav' were written, one might think a toshav eats, but a sakhir certainly does not. However, if only 'sakhir' were written, one might think a sakhir does not eat, but a toshav does. Therefore, both are needed.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara introduces a baraita about a toshav (acquired for eternity) and a sakhir (acquired for years) to illustrate a logical principle.
The Gemara poses a hypothetical: if only 'toshav' were written, one might infer by קל וחומר (a fortiori) that a sakhir certainly does not eat.

The Gemara explains that both terms are needed: without 'sakhir', one might mistakenly think 'toshav' refers to a short-term acquisition, so 'sakhir' teaches that even a permanent acquisition does not eat.

items.text: Abaye's objection to the analogy
items.text_en: Abaye's objection to the analogy
items.desc_en: Abaye objects that the cases are different: there, two separate entities are involved, and the verse could have been derived by kal vachomer, yet the Torah wrote it. Here, it is one entity: if she leaves during na'arut, what is bagrut doing with him?

sub.desc_en: Abaye objects that the cases are different: there, two separate entities are involved, and the verse could have been derived by kal vachomer, yet the Torah wrote it; here, it is one entity—if she leaves during na'arut, what is bagrut doing with him?

items.text: Abaye's answer: the case of an aylonit
items.text_en: Abaye's answer: the case of an aylonit
items.desc_en: Abaye explains that the verse is needed for an aylonit (a woman who does not develop signs of puberty). One might think she goes out during na'arut but not during bagrut, so the verse teaches that she does.

sub.desc_en: Abaye answers that the verse is needed for the bagrut (adulthood) of an aylonit (a woman who does not develop signs of puberty), teaching that she goes out from her father's authority at that stage.

items.text: Mar bar Rav Ashi's objection and alternative answer
items.text_en: Mar bar Rav Ashi's objection and alternative answer
items.desc_en: Mar bar Rav Ashi objects that bagrut should be derivable by kal vachomer from simanim (signs of puberty) that do not remove from the father's authority but do remove from the master's authority. He then offers his own answer: the verse is needed for the validity of the sale of an aylonit. One might think that if she develops signs of na'arut, the sale is valid, but if not, it is not, so the verse teaches otherwise.

sub.desc_en: Mar bar Rav Ashi objects that bagrut should be derivable by kal vachomer from simanim (signs of puberty) that do not remove from the father's authority but do remove from the master's authority.

sub.text: Mar bar Rav Ashi's alternative answer
sub.text_en: Mar bar Rav Ashi's alternative answer
sub.desc_en: Mar bar Rav Ashi offers his own answer: the verse is needed for the validity of the sale of an aylonit, teaching that even without signs of na'arut the sale is valid.

items.text: Gemara's response to Mar bar Rav Ashi's objection
items.text_en: Gemara's response to Mar bar Rav Ashi's objection
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the verse 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' teaches that a woman is acquired through money, and addresses Mar bar Rav Ashi's claim that this could be derived through a kal vachomer. The Gemara responds that a kal vachomer is written only when there is no possibility of refutation, but here there is a refutation, so the verse is necessary.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara states that the verse 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' teaches that a woman is acquired through money.
Mar bar Rav Ashi objects that the acquisition through money could be derived through a kal vachomer (a fortiori) argument, making the verse seemingly unnecessary.
The Gemara rejects the objection, explaining that a kal vachomer is written only when there is no possibility of refutation, but here there is a refutation, so the verse is necessary.

items.text: Derivation of acquisition through money from the verse 'כִּי יִקַּח'
items.text_en: Derivation of acquisition through money from the verse 'כִּי יִקַּח'
items.desc_en: The Tanna derives from the verse 'כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה' that acquisition (קִיחָה) is through money, as in the verse 'נָתַתִּי כֶּסֶף הַשָּׂדֶה קַח מִמֶּנִּי'. A kal vachomer from a Hebrew maidservant is proposed but refuted by yevama, and then a second refutation is offered. The verse 'כִּי יִקַּח' is needed to counter these refutations.

sub.desc_en: The baraita cites the verse 'כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה' to prove that acquisition (קִיחָה) is through money, supported by the verse 'נָתַתִּי כֶּסֶף הַשָּׂדֶה קַח מִמֶּנִּי'.

The Gemara proposes a kal vachomer (a fortiori inference): if a Hebrew maidservant, who cannot be acquired through intercourse, is acquired through money, then a woman, who can be acquired through intercourse, should certainly be acquired through money.

An objection is raised: a yevama (levirate widow) is acquired through intercourse but not through money, refuting the kal vachomer; however, the Gemara rejects this objection by noting that a yevama cannot be acquired through a document, unlike a woman who can.
The Gemara questions why a verse is needed if the kal vachomer already suffices, and Rav Ashi answers that a refutation exists from the outset.
Rav Ashi explains the refutation: a Hebrew maidservant can be released through money, but a woman cannot be divorced through money, so the kal vachomer fails, necessitating the verse 'כִּי יִקַּח'.

items.text: Necessity of both verses 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' and 'כִּי יִקַּח'
items.text_en: Necessity of both verses 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' and 'כִּי יִקַּח'
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that both verses are necessary: 'כִּי יִקַּח' alone would imply that the money given by the husband for betrothal belongs to the wife, so 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' teaches otherwise. Conversely, 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' alone might imply that if a woman gives money to a man and betroths him, it is valid, so 'כִּי יִקַּח' teaches that the man must take (acquire), not the woman.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara states that both verses 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' (then shall she go out for nothing) and 'כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ' (when a man takes) are necessary.
The Gemara explains that if only 'כִּי יִקַּח' were written, one might think the betrothal money given by the husband belongs to the wife, so 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' teaches otherwise.
The Gemara explains that if only 'וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם' were written, one might think a woman can betroth a man by giving money, so 'כִּי יִקַּח' teaches that the man must take, not the woman.

items.text: Derivation of acquisition through intercourse from the verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ'
items.text_en: Derivation of acquisition through intercourse from the verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ'
items.desc_en: The verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ' teaches that a woman is acquired through intercourse. A kal vachomer from yevama is proposed but refuted by a Hebrew maidservant. Rav Ashi explains that the verse is needed because there is a refutation from the start: yevama is already designated (זְקוּקָה וְעוֹמֶדֶת), unlike a regular woman. The verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ' is therefore necessary.

sub.desc_en: The verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ' (and engages in sexual intercourse with her) teaches that a woman is acquired through ביאה (intercourse), and a קל וחומר (a fortiori inference) from יבמה (a yevama) is proposed to support this.

The case of a Hebrew maidservant refutes the קל וחומר, since she is acquired through money yet not through intercourse, though the Gemara distinguishes that her acquisition is not for the sake of marriage.
The Gemara asks why the verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ' is needed at all, since the halakha could be derived through the קל וחומר.
Rav Ashi answers that the verse is necessary because the קל וחומר can be refuted from the outset, since the derivation is from יבמה.
The refutation is stated: what is unique about a יבמה is that she is זקוקה ועומדת (bound and waiting), unlike an ordinary woman, so the verse 'וּבְעָלָהּ' is required.

items.text: Initial attempt to derive betrothal by document from a kal va-ḥomer
items.text_en: Initial attempt to derive betrothal by document from a kal va-ḥomer
items.desc_en: The Gemara proposes a kal va-ḥomer: if money, which does not effect divorce, effects betrothal, then a document, which does effect divorce, should certainly effect betrothal. The objection is raised that money has a unique quality—it redeems consecrated property and second tithe—which a document lacks, as Scripture says 'and he shall give the money and it shall be his.'

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes a kal va-ḥomer (קל וחומר, a fortiori argument): if money, which does not effect divorce, effects betrothal, then a document, which does effect divorce, should certainly effect betrothal.

The objection is raised that money has a unique quality—it redeems consecrated property (הקדש) and second tithe (מעשר שני)—which a document lacks, as Scripture says 'וְנָתַן הַכֶּסֶף וְקָם לוֹ' (and he shall give the money and it shall be his).

items.text: Derivation from the analogy of 'going out' and 'being'
items.text_en: Derivation from the analogy of 'going out' and 'being'
items.desc_en: The Gemara offers a scriptural derivation: the Torah juxtaposes 'going out' (יציאה) and 'being' (הויה), teaching that just as divorce is by document, so too betrothal can be by document; and conversely, just as betrothal is by money, so too divorce can be by money.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the scriptural juxtaposition of 'וְיָצְאָה' (she goes out) and 'וְהָיְתָה' (she becomes) to derive a double analogy: betrothal (הויה) can be by document like divorce (יציאה), and divorce can be by money like betrothal.

items.text: Abaye's objection: the advocate becomes the accuser
items.text_en: Abaye's objection: the advocate becomes the accuser
items.desc_en: Abaye objects: if money both effects betrothal and divorce, then the same money that serves as an advocate (for betrothal) becomes an accuser (for divorce). The Gemara initially tries to distinguish between different money, but notes that currency is the same. This objection is left unresolved.

sub.desc_en: Abaye objects: if money both effects betrothal and divorce, people will say that the same money that advocates (for betrothal) becomes an accuser (for divorce), and similarly a document that divorces would become an advocate for betrothal.
The Gemara attempts to distinguish that each document or coin is separate, but concedes that currency is fundamentally the same, leaving the objection unresolved.

items.text: Rava's derivation: divorce by writing, not by money
items.text_en: Rava's derivation: divorce by writing, not by money
items.desc_en: Rava argues that the verse 'and he writes for her' implies divorce is by writing, not by money. The Gemara questions why this does not also exclude betrothal by writing, and answers that the analogy of 'going out' and 'being' already teaches that betrothal can be by writing. The Gemara then asks why we prioritize the exclusion of divorce by money over the exclusion of betrothal by writing, and answers that since the verse is in the context of divorce, it is more logical to exclude divorce by money.

sub.desc_en: Rava argues that the verse 'and he writes for her' implies divorce is by writing, not by money.
The Gemara questions why this does not also exclude betrothal by writing.
The Gemara answers that the analogy of 'going out' and 'being' already teaches that betrothal can be by writing.
The Gemara then asks why we prioritize the exclusion of divorce by money over the exclusion of betrothal by writing.
The Gemara answers that since the verse is in the context of divorce, it is more logical to exclude divorce by money.

items.text: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili's view and the meaning of 'sefer keritut'
items.text_en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili's view and the meaning of 'sefer keritut'
items.desc_en: For Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who uses the verse for another derivation, the exclusion of divorce by money comes from 'sefer keritut'—a document cuts her off, nothing else does. The Rabbis use 'keritut' to require a complete severance, as in a conditional divorce that is not permanent. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili derives this from the double expression 'karet keritut', while the Rabbis do not learn from that.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: For Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who uses the verse for another derivation, from where does he derive that a woman cannot be divorced by money?
The Gemara answers: The verse says 'ספר כריתת' (a book of severance) — a document severs her, and nothing else severs her.
The Gemara asks: And the Rabbis, what do they do with this word 'כריתת' (severance)?
The Gemara answers: It is needed for a matter that severs between him and her — a complete severance.

A baraita is cited: If one says 'This is your get on condition that you never drink wine' or 'never go to your father's house', this is not a complete severance; but if he says 'for thirty days', it is a complete severance.

The Gemara resolves: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili derives the requirement of complete severance from the double expression 'כרת כריתת' (cutting off of severance), while the Rabbis do not learn from that double expression.

items.text: Attempts to derive betrothal by document from two other modes
items.text_en: Attempts to derive betrothal by document from two other modes
items.desc_en: The Gemara considers deriving betrothal by document from two other modes (e.g., money and intercourse) since one alone is insufficient. Each proposed derivation is rejected: from money and intercourse because their benefit is greater; from document and intercourse because their acquisition is greater; from document and money because they can be done against her will, but money also has that quality in the case of a Hebrew maidservant, though not in marriage.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes deriving betrothal by document from two other modes (money and intercourse) since one alone was insufficient.
The first proposed derivation (from money and intercourse) is rejected because their benefit (הנאתן מרובה) is greater than that of a document.
The second proposed derivation (from document and intercourse) is rejected because their acquisition (קנינן מרובה) is greater than that of money.
The third proposed derivation (from document and money) is rejected because they can be done against her will (ישנן בעל כרחה), but money also has that quality in the case of a Hebrew maidservant.
The Gemara responds that although money can be used against her will for a Hebrew maidservant, in the context of marriage (באישות) we do not find such a case, so the objection stands.

items.text: Rav Huna's kal va-ḥomer for ḥuppah and the discussion of terumah
items.text_en: Rav Huna's kal va-ḥomer for ḥuppah and the discussion of terumah
items.desc_en: Rav Huna proposes that ḥuppah (the wedding canopy) effects betrothal via a kal va-ḥomer from money: if money, which does not permit eating terumah, effects betrothal, then ḥuppah, which does permit eating terumah, should certainly effect betrothal. The Gemara objects that according to Torah law, an arusah does eat terumah, and the rabbinic prohibition is a decree. The Gemara then reframes the kal va-ḥomer: money, which does not complete the marriage (as it can be undone by divorce), effects betrothal; ḥuppah, which completes the marriage, should certainly effect betrothal.

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna proposes that חופה (the wedding canopy) effects betrothal via a kal va-ḥomer from money: if money, which does not permit eating תרומה (priestly portion), effects betrothal, then חופה, which does permit eating תרומה, should certainly effect betrothal.
The Gemara objects that money does permit eating תרומה, citing Ulla that by Torah law an arusah (betrothed woman) eats תרומה, as she is a 'קִנְיַן כַּסְפּוֹ' (acquisition of his money).
The Gemara explains that the rabbinic prohibition against the arusah eating תרומה is a decree (גזירה) lest she pour a cup of wine for her brother or sister in her father's house.

The Gemara reframes the kal va-ḥomer: money, which does not complete the marriage (as it can be undone by divorce), effects betrothal; חופה, which completes the marriage, should certainly effect betrothal.

items.text: Gemara's binyan av to include chuppah
items.text_en: Gemara's binyan av to include chuppah
items.desc_en: The Gemara attempts to derive chuppah as a mode of kiddushin through a binyan av from kesef and bi'ah, but the argument is refuted because the common denominator (tzad hashaveh) has the flaw that both kesef and bi'ah involve great benefit (hana'atan merubah). The Gemara then tries to include chuppah via a second binyan av that includes shtar, but that too is refuted.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara proposes a logical argument that a wedding canopy (חופה) should effect betrothal because it completes the marriage, and then rejects the analogy to money by noting that money has unique properties (redeeming consecrated property and second tithe).

The Gemara counters that intercourse (ביאה) proves otherwise, as it acquires a woman despite not being a general mode of acquisition, and then constructs a common denominator (צד השוה) between money and intercourse to include chuppah.

The Gemara objects that the common denominator of money and intercourse involves great benefit (הנאתן מרובה), and then introduces a document (שטר) as a counterexample, but notes that a document can release a woman, which money and intercourse cannot.

The Gemara returns to the common denominator argument, concluding that since all three modes (money, intercourse, document) generally effect acquisition and effect acquisition here, chuppah should also effect betrothal.

items.text: Rav Huna's objection: kesef is not acquired against her will in marriage
items.text_en: Rav Huna's objection: kesef is not acquired against her will in marriage
items.desc_en: Rav Huna points out that the common denominator of the binyan av is flawed because kesef is not acquired against the woman's will in marriage (be'al korchah), unlike in hekdesh and ma'aser sheni.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects to the common denominator of the binyan av by noting that all three modes (kesef, shtar, bi'ah) are effective against her will, which chuppah is not.
Rav Huna responds that in any event, with regard to marriage (ishut) we have not found kesef acquiring a woman against her will, so the objection does not undermine the derivation for chuppah.

items.text: Rava's two refutations of the binyan av
items.text_en: Rava's two refutations of the binyan av
items.desc_en: Rava offers two decisive refutations: first, the Mishnah explicitly lists only three modes (shalosh t'nan) and not four; second, chuppah only completes marriage after kiddushin, so we cannot learn chuppah without kiddushin from chuppah with kiddushin.

sub.desc_en: Rava raises two objections: first, the Mishnah teaches 'three' modes of acquisition, not 'four'; second, chuppah only completes betrothal after kiddushin, so how can we derive chuppah without prior kiddushin from chuppah with kiddushin?
Rava argues that the Mishnah explicitly lists only three modes of kiddushin (שלוש), not four, so chuppah cannot be added.
Rava argues that chuppah only completes marriage after kiddushin, so we cannot derive chuppah without kiddushin from chuppah with kiddushin.

items.text: Abaye's defense of Rav Huna
items.text_en: Abaye's defense of Rav Huna
items.desc_en: Abaye defends Rav Huna against Rava's refutations: the Mishnah only states what is explicit in the Torah, and Rav Huna's argument was actually a kal vachomer from kesef to chuppah, not a binyan av.

sub.desc_en: Abaye responds to Rava's objections: the Tanna only lists explicitly written modes, not derived ones; and Rav Huna's argument is that just as money, which does not complete after money, acquires, so chuppah, which completes after money, should certainly acquire.
Abaye responds to Rava's second objection: Rav Huna's argument was actually a קל וחומר (a fortiori inference) from כסף (money) to חופה (canopy), not a בנין אב (constructive precedent).

items.text: Tanna's baraita on the formula for kiddushin with money
items.text_en: Tanna's baraita on the formula for kiddushin with money
items.desc_en: A baraita teaches that if a man gives money and says the correct formula (e.g., 'harei at mekudeshet li'), she is betrothed; but if she gives money and says the formula, she is not betrothed.

sub.desc_en: A baraita is cited explaining how betrothal with money works: if he gives money and says the appropriate formula, she is betrothed; but if she gives and speaks, she is not betrothed.

items.text: Rav Pappa's challenge and resolution of the baraita's contradiction
items.text_en: Rav Pappa's challenge and resolution of the baraita's contradiction
items.desc_en: Rav Pappa points out an internal contradiction in the baraita: the first clause implies that if he gives and she speaks, she is not betrothed, but the second clause implies the opposite. The Gemara resolves by reinterpreting the baraita: either the first clause is precise and the second is a scribal error, or the baraita means that if he gives and she speaks, it is a safek and we are concerned.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa challenges the baraita by pointing out an internal contradiction: the first clause implies that if he gives and she speaks, she is not betrothed, but the second clause implies the opposite.
The Gemara objects: the first clause is precise, but the second clause is taken as a scribal error, yet it contradicts the first.
The Gemara resolves: the baraita means that if he gives and he speaks, she is betrothed; if he gives and she speaks, it is as if she gave and she spoke, so she is not betrothed.

Alternatively, the Gemara resolves: if he gives and he speaks, she is betrothed; if she gives and she speaks, she is not; if he gives and she speaks, it is a safek (doubt) and we are concerned rabbinically.

items.text: Shmuel's ruling on the formula for kiddushin and get
items.text_en: Shmuel's ruling on the formula for kiddushin and get
items.desc_en: Shmuel rules that for kiddushin, if the man says 'harei at mekudeshet' etc., she is betrothed; but if he says 'hareini ishekh' etc., there is no concern. Similarly for divorce, if he says 'harei at meshulachat' etc., she is divorced; but if he says 'eini ishekh' etc., there is no concern.

sub.desc_en: Shmuel rules that for betrothal, if the man gives money and says 'הרי את מקודשת' (you are betrothed) etc., she is betrothed; but if he says 'הריני אישך' (I am your man) etc., there is no concern.

Shmuel adds that similarly for divorce, if the husband gives a bill of divorce and says 'הרי את משולחת' (you are sent away) etc., she is divorced; but if he says 'איני אישך' (I am not your man) etc., there is no concern.

items.text: Rav Pappa's question on Shmuel's view of 'yadayim she'ein mochichot'
items.text_en: Rav Pappa's question on Shmuel's view of 'yadayim she'ein mochichot'
items.desc_en: Rav Pappa asks Abaye whether Shmuel holds that 'yadayim she'ein mochichot' (incomplete speech acts) are considered valid, citing a contradiction from Shmuel's own ruling on a nazirite vow. The Gemara answers that here Shmuel's case involves the word 'li', which provides sufficient context.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa asks Abaye whether Shmuel holds that ambiguous intimations (יָדַיִם שֶׁאֵין מוֹכִיחוֹת) are considered valid.
Rav Pappa cites a mishna (Nazir 2a) where Shmuel rules that 'I shall be' only makes one a nazirite if a nazirite passes before him, showing that ambiguous intimations are not valid without context.
The Gemara answers that Shmuel's case in betrothal involves the word 'לִי' (to me), which provides sufficient context, distinguishing it from the nazirite case.

items.text: הבחנה בין לשונות קניין לעצמו
items.text_en: Gemara's inference from the verses
items.desc_en: The Gemara explains that the verses 'כי יקח' and 'ושלחה' imply that a man cannot betroth or divorce himself, only others.
items.desc: הגמרא מסבירה ששמואל מלמד שהביטויים 'הרי אני' אינם מועילים לקדושין או לגירושין, משום שהפסוקים מדגישים פעולה על האישה ולא על עצמו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers from the verses 'כי יקח' and 'ושלחה' that a man cannot betroth or divorce himself, only others.
sub.desc: הגמרא מסבירה ששמואל מלמד שהביטויים 'כי יקח' ו'ושלחה' אינם כוללים מעשה עצמי, ולכן אין לחשוש לביטויים כמו 'אני לך' או 'איני שלך'.

items.text: ברייתא: לשונות קידושין
items.text_en: Baraita listing valid betrothal terms
items.desc_en: A baraita lists six terms that effect betrothal: 'אשתי', 'ארוסתי', 'קנויה לי', 'שלי', 'ברשותי', 'זקוקה לי'. The Gemara notes that the Tanna taught them in two groups of three for memorization.
items.desc: ברייתא מונה שש לשונות קידושין, המחולקות לשתי קבוצות של שלוש, וכולן מקדשות. הגמרא שואלת מדוע לא נשנו יחד, ועונה שהתנא שמע אותן כשתי קבוצות נפרדות.

sub.desc_en: The baraita lists six terms that effect betrothal: 'אשתי', 'ארוסתי', 'קנויה לי', 'שלי', 'ברשותי', 'זקוקה לי'.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בקבוצת הביטויים הראשונה: 'הרי את אשתי', 'הרי את ארוסתי', 'הרי את קנויה לי' – האומר אחד מאלה מקודשת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks why the Tanna did not teach all six terms together in one list.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בקבוצת הביטויים הראשונה: 'הרי את אשתי', 'הרי את ארוסתי', 'הרי את קנויה לי' – האומר אחד מאלה מקודשת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers that the Tanna taught them in two groups of three for ease of memorization.
sub.desc: הברייתא פותחת בקבוצת הביטויים הראשונה: 'הרי את אשתי', 'הרי את ארוסתי', 'הרי את קנויה לי' – האומר אחד מאלה מקודשת.

items.text: בעיות בלשונות קידושין נוספות
items.text_en: Inquiry about additional terms and resolution for 'לקוחתי'
items.desc_en: The Gemara raises a series of unresolved questions about other terms like 'מיוחדת', 'מיועדת', etc. It then resolves one: 'לקוחתי' effects betrothal based on the verse 'כי יקח איש אשה'.
items.desc: הגמרא מעלה ספקות לגבי לשונות נוספים כמו 'מיוחדת לי', 'מיועדת לי', 'עזרתי' וכו', ופושטת לפחות אחת מהן: 'לקוחתי' מקדשת משום שנאמר 'כי יקח איש אשה'.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara raises unresolved questions about whether various terms like 'מיוחדת', 'מיועדת', 'עזרתי', etc., effect betrothal.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה ספקות לגבי ביטויים שונים שאומר אדם לאשה, האם הם לשון קידושין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves one of the questions: the term 'לקוחתי' effects betrothal, citing the verse 'כי יקח איש אשה' (for a man takes a wife).
sub.desc: הגמרא פושטת ספק אחד: האומר 'לקוחתי' מקודשת, שנאמר 'כי יקח איש אשה'.

items.text: חרופתי: לשון מקובלת ביהודה
items.text_en: Inquiry about 'חרופתי' and resolution
items.desc_en: The Gemara asks about 'חרופתי'. It first suggests a proof from Judean usage, but questions whether Judah constitutes the majority. It then refines the answer: 'חרופתי' is valid based on the verse 'והיא שפחה נחרפת לאיש', and in Judah it is also a common term for betrothal.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה בלשון 'חרופתי', ומביאה ברייתא שמקדשת, תחילה על סמך לשון יהודה, ואחר כך על סמך פסוק. הגמרא מבהירה שההיתר הוא דווקא ביהודה, שם לשון זו מובנת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara inquires whether the term 'חרופתי' (my designated one) is effective for betrothal.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה את השאלה האם האומר 'חרופתי' מקדש.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites a baraita that rules 'חרופתי' is effective for betrothal, based on Judean usage where 'חרופה' means betrothed.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה את השאלה האם האומר 'חרופתי' מקדש.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Judean usage alone cannot establish a universal rule, since Judah is not the majority of the world.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה את השאלה האם האומר 'חרופתי' מקדש.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves that the baraita's ruling is based on the verse 'והיא שפחה נחרפת לאיש' (a maid designated for a man), with Judean usage as additional support, and clarifies that the ruling applies specifically in Judah.
sub.desc: הגמרא מעלה את השאלה האם האומר 'חרופתי' מקדש.

items.text: הקשר השיחה והבנת הכוונה
items.text_en: Discussion of context: speaking about the get or kiddushin
items.desc_en: The Gemara analyzes the scenario of the baraita: if the man is not speaking about the get or kiddushin, the woman doesn't know his intent; if he is, even without explicit terms it might suffice. It cites the dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehuda, and concludes with a teiku for the ambiguous terms.
items.desc: הגמרא מבררת שהספקות לגבי הלשונות נאמרו במקרה שהיה מדבר עמה על עסקי גיטין וקידושין, ואז אם נתן לה כסף ושתק, היא מקודשת. כאן מדובר שנתן לה ואמר לה לשון מסוימת, והספק הוא אם התכוון לקדושין או לשכירות.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: what context are we dealing with? If the man is not speaking about the get or kiddushin, how would the woman know his intent?
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת באיזה מקרה מדובר בביטויים אלו: אם לא דיבר עמה על עסקי גיטין וקידושין, היא לא יודעת למה התכוון; ואם דיבר עמה, אפילו בלא אמירה היא מקודשת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara answers: if he is speaking about the get or kiddushin, even without explicit terms it might suffice.
sub.desc: הגמרא שואלת באיזה מקרה מדובר בביטויים אלו: אם לא דיבר עמה על עסקי גיטין וקידושין, היא לא יודעת למה התכוון; ואם דיבר עמה, אפילו בלא אמירה היא מקודשת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the baraita: if a man was speaking about the get or kiddushin and gave the item without specifying, Rabbi Yosei says it is sufficient, Rabbi Yehuda says he must specify, and Rav Huna said Shmuel ruled like Rabbi Yosei.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה משנה שבה נחלקו רבי יוסי ורבי יהודה אם צריך לפרש כשנתן גט או קידושין תוך כדי שיחה על עסקיהם, ופסק שמואל כרבי יוסי שדי בכך.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves: actually, he is speaking about the get or kiddushin, but here he gave it and said these ambiguous terms.
sub.desc: הגמרא מתרצת: אכן מדובר כשדיבר עמה על עסקי גיטין וקידושין, ואם נתן ושתק היתה מקודשת, אבל כאן מדובר שנתן לה ואמר לה אחד מהביטויים הללו.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: do these terms mean kiddushin or perhaps they mean employment? The question remains unresolved (תיקו).
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שהספק הוא אם הביטויים נאמרו לשם קידושין או לשם מלאכה, ומסיימת בתיקו.

items.text: The condition of being engaged in the same topic
items.text_en: The condition of being engaged in the same topic
items.desc_en: The Gemara revisits the Mishnah and adds that Rabbi Yosei's ruling applies only when they are engaged in that topic. This is supported by Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel, Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Oshaya, and a Tannaitic dispute. Abaye explains that even if not directly discussing, the context can indicate intent.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara cites the Mishnah about a man speaking with a woman about her divorce or betrothal, where Rabbi Yosei says it is sufficient and Rabbi Yehuda says he must specify.

sub.text: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel
sub.text_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel
sub.desc_en: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel adds the condition that Rabbi Yosei's ruling applies only when they are engaged in that same topic.

sub.text: Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Oshaya
sub.text_en: Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Oshaya
sub.desc_en: Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Oshaya similarly states the condition that they must be engaged in that same topic.
A Tannaitic dispute is cited: Rabbi requires that they be engaged in that same topic, while Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon holds that even if they are not engaged in that topic, it is sufficient.
The Gemara questions how the woman would know what he is saying if they are not engaged in that topic.
Abaye answers that even if they are not directly discussing, the context can indicate intent, as they move from one topic to another within the same general subject.

items.text: Halakhic ruling and parallel for divorce
items.text_en: Halakhic ruling and parallel for divorce
items.desc_en: Rav Huna in the name of Shmuel rules like Rabbi Yosei. Rav Yemar asks Rav Ashi about the consistency with another statement of Shmuel, and Rav Ashi confirms. The Gemara then lists valid divorce terms, and notes that if one says 'הרי את בת חורין' it is obvious.

sub.desc_en: Rav Huna in the name of Shmuel rules that the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei regarding the need to specify the intent when giving a get or kiddushin while already discussing that topic.
Rav Yemar asks Rav Ashi whether Shmuel's statement that one who does not understand the details of gittin and kiddushin should not engage in them contradicts Shmuel's ruling through Rav Huna.
Rav Ashi confirms that Shmuel's two statements are consistent and that the halacha indeed follows Rabbi Yosei.
The Gemara lists valid divorce terms that effect a get, paralleling the earlier list for kiddushin.
The Gemara notes that if one gives a get and says 'you are a free woman' (בת חורין), the divorce is obviously valid, as it implies release from the marriage bond.

items.text: Opening ruling on ineffective divorce language
items.text_en: Opening ruling on ineffective divorce language
items.desc_en: The Gemara states that saying 'you are permitted to any man' to one's maidservant or wife accomplishes nothing, as it lacks the force of a valid get or manumission.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens with a ruling that saying 'you are permitted to any man' to a maidservant or wife is ineffective.

items.text: Question on 'you are for yourself' and proof from slave manumission
items.text_en: Question on 'you are for yourself' and proof from slave manumission
items.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether saying 'you are for yourself' to one's wife means for work or full divorce. Ravina brings a baraita that 'you are for yourself' is the body of a manumission document, arguing that if it frees a slave, it certainly divorces a wife.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions whether saying 'you are for yourself' to one's wife means for work or for full divorce.
Ravina cites a baraita that 'you are for yourself' is the body of a manumission document, arguing that if it frees a slave, it certainly divorces a wife.

items.text: ביטוי 'אין לי עסק בך' לעבד
items.text_en: Question on 'I have no business with you' and proof from sale to a gentile
items.desc_en: Ravina asks about saying 'I have no business with you' to a slave. Rav Nachman cites a baraita that selling a slave to a gentile frees him and requires a get, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says if the seller wrote 'when you flee from him, I have no business with you', that is his manumission.
items.desc: הגמרא שואלת אם אמירה 'אין לי עסק בך' לעבד משחררת אותו. רב נחמן מביא ברייתא על מוכר עבדו לנכרי, ורשב"ג אומר שאם כתב לו 'כשתמלט אין לי עסק בך' זהו שחרורו, מה שמוכיח שהביטוי משחרר.

sub.desc_en: Ravina asks Rav Ashi whether saying 'אין לי עסק בך' (I have no business with you) to a slave means complete emancipation or merely release from labor.
sub.desc: רבינא שואל את רב אשי: אם אדם אומר לעבדו 'אין לי עסק בך', האם הכוונה לשחררו לגמרי או רק לפטרו ממלאכה?

sub.text: Rav Nachman's answer to Rav Ashi
sub.text_en: Rav Nachman's answer to Rav Ashi
sub.desc_en: Rav Nachman cites a baraita that selling a slave to a gentile frees him and requires a גט שחרור (bill of manumission) from the first master.

sub.text: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's ruling and Rav Sheshet's explanation
sub.text_en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's ruling and Rav Sheshet's explanation
sub.desc_en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel rules that if the seller wrote 'כשתבח ממנו אין לי עסק בך' (when you flee from him, I have no business with you), that document itself is his emancipation, and Rav Sheshet explains that this shows the phrase 'אין לי עסק בך' (I have no business with you) is a valid expression of manumission.

items.text: קידושין במלווה ובהנאת מלווה
items.text_en: Abaye on betrothal with a loan and its benefit
items.desc_en: Abaye rules that betrothal with a loan is invalid, but with the benefit of a loan (e.g., extending time) it is valid, though prohibited due to interest. The Gemara clarifies that the benefit is not direct interest but granting extra time.
items.desc: אביי פוסק שמקדש במלווה אינה מקודשת, אבל בהנאת מלווה מקודשת, ואסור לעשות כן משום הערמת ריבית. הגמרא מבהירה שהמדובר בהארכת זמן, שזו הנאה האסורה כריבית.

sub.desc_en: Abaye rules that betrothal with a loan is invalid, but with the benefit of a loan it is valid, though prohibited due to interest.
The Gemara asks what constitutes the benefit of a loan, and rejects the possibility that it refers to direct interest, which would still be a loan.
The Gemara clarifies that the benefit is not direct interest but granting extra time for repayment, which is a valid benefit for betrothal.

items.text: מתנה על מנת להחזיר: דין רבא והבחנת רב אשי
items.text_en: Rava's ruling on conditional gift and Rav Ashi's resolution
items.desc_en: Rava rules that giving money on condition of return is ineffective for sale, betrothal, and redemption of the firstborn, but valid for terumah. The Gemara questions Rava's consistency, and Rav Ashi explains that all cases except betrothal work, since a woman cannot be acquired through exchange (חליפין). Rav Huna Mar bar Rav Nechemya confirms this from Rava's tradition.
items.desc: רבא דן במתנה על מנת להחזיר: במכר, באשה, בפדיון הבן ובתרומה. הגמרא מקשה על רבא, ומתרצת בשם רב אשי שבכולם קנה חוץ מאשה, שאינה נקנית בחליפין.

sub.desc_en: Rava rules that giving money on condition of return is ineffective for sale, betrothal, and redemption of the firstborn, but valid for terumah, though prohibited due to appearance of a priest assisting at the granary.
sub.desc: רבא פוסק: מתנה על מנת להחזיר אינה מועילה במכר, באשה ובפדיון הבן, אבל בתרומה יוצא ידי נתינה, ואסור לעשות כן לכתחילה.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara questions Rava's consistency: if he holds that a conditional gift is a valid gift, all cases should work; if not, even terumah should fail.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה: אם רבא סובר שמתנה על מנת להחזיר שמה מתנה, היה צריך להועיל בכל המקרים; ואם לאו, גם בתרומה לא תועיל.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects that Rava himself elsewhere ruled that a conditional gift is a valid gift, citing his ruling about an etrog given on condition of return.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה עוד: הרי רבא בעצמו אמר שמתנה על מנת להחזיר שמה מתנה, כפי שמוכח מדין אתרוג.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi resolves that all cases except betrothal work, since a woman cannot be acquired through exchange (חליפין), and Rav Huna Mar bar Rav Nechemya confirms this from Rava's tradition.
sub.desc: רב אשי מתרץ: בכולם קנה חוץ מאשה, שאינה נקנית בחליפין; ורב הונא מר בריה דרב נחמיה מעיד שכך אמר רבא.

items.text: פתיחת סוגיה חדשה: 'תן מנה לפלוני'
items.text_en: Beginning of a new statement by Rava
items.desc_en: Rava begins a new ruling about giving a mane to someone, which continues on the next amud.
items.desc: רבא מתחיל דין חדש בנושא 'תן מנה לפלוני', כנראה בהקשר של קידושין או קניינים, אך הדיון נקטע כאן.

sub.desc_en: Rava begins a new ruling about giving a mane (a coin) to someone, which continues on the next amud.
sub.desc: רבא פותח דין חדש בנושא 'תן מנה לפלוני', כנראה בהקשר של קידושין או קניינים, אך הדיון נקטע כאן.

items.text: קידושין על ידי נתינת כסף לאחר – דין ערב ועבד כנעני
items.text_en: Analogy to an Arev and a Canaanite Slave
items.desc_en: The Gemara analyzes three cases of kiddushin through agency, comparing each to the laws of an arev (guarantor) or a Canaanite slave. It then raises objections to the analogies, showing that each comparison has a flaw, and the Gemara resolves by cross-referencing the two analogies.
items.desc: הגמרא דנה במקרה שבו האיש נותן כסף לאחר ואומר לאשה 'התקדשי לי בכסף שנתתי לפלוני', ודנה אם היא מקודשת. היא גוזרת זאת מדין ערב (שמשעבד עצמו אף ללא הנאה) ומדין עבד כנעני (שקונה את עצמו בכסף שאחרים נותנים עבורו). הגמרא דוחה כל אחת מההיקשים בנפרד, אך משלבת אותם כדי לבסס את הדין.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by establishing that a woman who says 'I will be betrothed to you' through a messenger is betrothed, drawing an analogy to an arev (guarantor) who obligates himself despite receiving no benefit.
sub.desc: הגמרא פותחת במקרה שבו האיש אומר לאשה 'התקדשי לי במנה שנתתי לפלוני', ודנה אם היא מקודשת, וגוזרת זאת מדין ערב.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara adds a second analogy: a woman who receives money to be betrothed to another is betrothed, like a Canaanite slave who acquires himself without losing anything.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה דין עבד כנעני, שקונה את עצמו בכסף שאחרים נותנים עבורו, ומקישה ממנו לאשה שמתקדשת בכסף שנתן אחר.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara presents a third case: a woman who says 'Give a maneh to so-and-so and I will be betrothed to him' is betrothed, combining both analogies.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה מקרה נוסף שבו האיש אומר 'תן מנה לפלוני ואקדש אני לך', ודנה אם היא מקודשת, וגוזרת מדין ערב ועבד כנעני גם יחד.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects to the first analogy: the guarantor's beneficiary loses money, but the man in the betrothal case loses nothing, so the Canaanite slave analogy is proposed as a better comparison.
sub.desc: הגמרא מקשה על ההיקש לערב: בערב, המלווה חסר ממון, אבל כאן האיש אינו חסר כלום; ומקשה על ההיקש לעבד כנעני: בעבד, הקונה חסר ממון, אבל כאן האישה אינה חסרה כלום.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara objects to the second analogy: in the slave case the acquirer also acquires, but here the woman gives herself without acquiring anything, so the guarantor analogy is reinstated.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את הקושיות: בערב, אף שאינו חסר ממון, הוא משעבד את עצמו; ובעבד, אף שאינו חסר ממון, הוא קונה את עצמו. לכן ההיקש תקף.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara resolves by cross-referencing the two analogies, concluding that the guarantor analogy proves the point despite the objection.
sub.desc: הגמרא דוחה את הקושיות: בערב, אף שאינו חסר ממון, הוא משעבד את עצמו; ובעבד, אף שאינו חסר ממון, הוא קונה את עצמו. לכן ההיקש תקף.

items.text: שאלת רבא: 'הילך מנה ואקדש אני לך'
items.text_en: Rava's Question: Woman Gives Money and Says 'Be Sanctified to Me'
items.desc_en: Rava asks about a case where a woman gives a man money and says 'be sanctified to me.' Mar Zutra in the name of Rav Pappa rules she is sanctified. Rav Ashi objects based on a mishna about property acquisition, and Mar Zutra explains that the case involves an important person, where the woman's benefit from giving a gift causes her to transfer herself.
items.desc: רבא שואל מה הדין אם האשה אומרת 'הילך מנה ואקדש אני לך'. מר זוטרא בשם רב פפא פוסק שמקודשת. רב אשי מקשה שזה נראה כקניין של דבר שאין בו אחריות עם דבר שיש לו אחריות, דבר שאינו תקף. מר זוטרא מתרץ שמדובר באדם חשוב, וההנאה מכך שהוא מקבל מתנה גורמת לה להקנות עצמו.

sub.desc_en: Rava asks about the case where a woman gives a man money and says 'be sanctified to me' — what is the halacha?
sub.desc: רבא שואל: האומר 'הילך מנה ואקדש אני לך' – מה דינה? ומר זוטרא משמיה דרב פפא עונה שהיא מקודשת.

sub.text_en: Mar Zutra in the name of Rav Pappa
sub.desc_en: Mar Zutra in the name of Rav Pappa rules that she is sanctified.
sub.desc: רבא שואל: האומר 'הילך מנה ואקדש אני לך' – מה דינה? ומר זוטרא משמיה דרב פפא עונה שהיא מקודשת.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi objects that if so, the ruling would reverse the mishnaic principle that property with a lien is acquired together with property without a lien.
sub.desc: רב אשי מקשה: אם כך, נמצא שדבר שאין לו אחריות (המעות) נקנה עם דבר שיש לו אחריות (האשה), בניגוד למשנתנו שדווקא דבר שאין לו אחריות נקנה עם דבר שיש לו אחריות.

sub.desc_en: Mar Zutra clarifies that the mishna teaches the opposite, and explains that the case involves an important person (אדם חשוב), where the woman's benefit from giving a gift causes her to transfer herself.
sub.desc: רב אשי מקשה: אם כך, נמצא שדבר שאין לו אחריות (המעות) נקנה עם דבר שיש לו אחריות (האשה), בניגוד למשנתנו שדווקא דבר שאין לו אחריות נקנה עם דבר שיש לו אחריות.

items.text: השלמה: דין זה נאמר גם לעניין ממון
items.text_en: Application to Monetary Law and Need for Both Teachings
items.desc_en: The Gemara states that Rava's ruling applies also to monetary law. It explains why both the case of kiddushin and the case of monetary law are necessary: kiddushin alone might be assumed to be lenient because a woman prefers any marriage (as per Resh Lakish), while monetary law alone might be assumed to be lenient because money can be forgiven.
items.desc: הגמרא מציינת שנאמר בשם רבא שדין זה (של קניין על ידי נתינת כסף לאחר) תקף גם לענייני ממון. יש צורך להשמיע זאת בשני ההקשרים: לגבי קידושין, כי אשה נוח לה בכל דהו, ולגבי ממון, כי ממון ניתן למחילה. לכן יש צורך בשני המקרים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara reports that Rava's ruling about the woman being betrothed when she says 'take this mane and I will be betrothed to you' applies also to monetary law.
sub.desc: הגמרא מציינת שנאמר בשם רבא שדין זה תקף גם לענייני ממון, ומוסיפה שיש צורך להשמיע זאת.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara explains that both the case of kiddushin and the case of monetary law are necessary: kiddushin alone might be assumed to be lenient because a woman prefers any marriage (as per Resh Lakish), while monetary law alone might be assumed to be lenient because money can be forgiven.
sub.desc: הגמרא מסבירה מדוע היה צורך להשמיע דין זה לגבי קידושין: משום שאשה נוח לה בכל דהו, כדברי ריש לקיש, אבל לגבי ממון הייתי אומר שלא.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that both teachings are necessary: monetary law alone might be assumed to be lenient because money can be forgiven, but kiddushin might not be lenient, so both are needed.
sub.desc: הגמרא מוסיפה שאם היה משמיע רק לגבי ממון, הייתי אומר שדווקא שם הדין תקף משום שממון ניתן למחילה, אבל לגבי קידושין לא; לכן יש צורך בשני המקרים.

items.text: קידושין בחצי האיש או בחצי האישה
items.text_en: Rava's Ruling on Partial Kiddushin
items.desc_en: Rava rules that if a man says 'be sanctified to me for half of me,' she is sanctified, but if he says 'half of you is sanctified to me,' she is not sanctified. Abaye questions the distinction, arguing that just as the Torah requires a full woman, it requires a full man. Rava responds that a woman is not fit for two men, but a man is fit for two women, so the man's statement implies he may marry another.
items.desc: רבא פוסק: אם האיש אומר 'התקדשי לי לחציי' – מקודשת, כי הוא יכול לשאת אשה אחרת. אבל אם הוא אומר 'חצייך מקודשת לי' – אינה מקודשת, כי התורה אמרה 'אשה' ולא חצי אשה. אביי מקשה: אם כן, גם 'איש' ולא חצי איש? רבא עונה: אין דומה, כי אשה אינה ראויה לשני אנשים, אבל איש ראוי לשתי נשים.

sub.desc_en: Rava rules that if a man says 'be sanctified to me for half of me,' she is sanctified, but if he says 'half of you is sanctified to me,' she is not sanctified.
sub.desc: רבא פוסק: האומר 'התקדשי לי לחציי' – מקודשת, אבל 'חצייך מקודשת לי' – אינה מקודשת.

sub.desc_en: Abaye objects that just as the Torah requires a full woman (אישה) and not half a woman, it also requires a full man (איש) and not half a man, so both cases should be invalid.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה: אם בחצי אשה אינה מקודשת משום 'אשה' ולא חצי אשה, גם בחצי איש נאמר 'איש' ולא חצי איש?

sub.desc_en: Rava distinguishes: a woman is not fit for two men, but a man is fit for two women, so when he says 'half of me,' he implies he may marry another, making the kiddushin valid.
sub.desc: אביי מקשה: אם בחצי אשה אינה מקודשת משום 'אשה' ולא חצי אשה, גם בחצי איש נאמר 'איש' ולא חצי איש?

items.text: Mar Zutra's Objection and Resolution via Rabbi Yochanan
items.text_en: Mar Zutra's Objection and Resolution via Rabbi Yochanan
items.desc_en: Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari objects to Rava's ruling, citing a baraita about consecrating an animal's limb. The Gemara distinguishes between consecration and kiddushin because kiddushin involves another person's intent. It then compares to Rabbi Yochanan's case of a shared animal, where partial consecration is effective but the animal cannot be offered.

sub.text: Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari to Ravina
sub.text_en: Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari to Ravina
sub.desc_en: Mar Zutra bar Rav Mari objects to Ravina: why not extend the kiddushin to the entire woman, citing a baraita where consecrating an animal's limb makes the whole animal a burnt-offering.
The Gemara clarifies that even for the opinion that the whole animal is not consecrated, that applies only to a non-vital limb, but a vital limb consecrates the entire animal.
The Gemara rejects the analogy: there the object is an animal, but here kiddushin involves another person's intent (דעת אחרת), which limits the effect.

The Gemara resolves the objection by comparing to Rabbi Yochanan's case: a shared animal where one partner consecrates his half and later buys the other half and consecrates it — the animal is consecrated but not offered, and it can effect temurah.

items.text: Conclusion: Three Halakhot Derived
items.text_en: Conclusion: Three Halakhot Derived
items.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that from Rabbi Yochanan's statement, three halakhot are derived, though the daf does not specify them here.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara concludes that from Rabbi Yochanan's statement, three halakhot are derived, though the daf does not specify them here.

items.text: הוכחה מדין בעלי חיים שנדחו
items.text_en: Inference from earlier case
items.desc_en: The Gemara infers three principles from the earlier mishnah: that living animals can be pushed aside (for sacrifice), that a disqualification from the outset is considered permanently disqualified, and that there is a concept of rejection regarding blood.
items.desc: הגמרא מסיקה מהמשנה שדחוי בבעלי חיים נחשב דחוי מעיקרו, ושדין דיחוי חל גם על דמים. זהו פתיח לדיון בספקות הבאים.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara infers three principles from the earlier mishnah: that living animals can be pushed aside (for sacrifice), that a disqualification from the outset is considered permanently disqualified, and that there is a concept of rejection regarding blood.
sub.desc: הגמרא מסיקה מהמשנה שדחוי בבעלי חיים נחשב דחוי מעיקרו, ושדין דיחוי חל גם על דמים.

items.text: ספקות רבא בקידושין בחצאין
items.text_en: Rava's series of unresolved questions on partial betrothal
items.desc_en: Rava poses a series of questions about betrothal with partial sums: whether saying 'half of you with a half-prutah' constitutes a fixed amount or ongoing counting, and similar variations. The series ends with the question of betrothing 'two halves of you with a prutah' and concludes with 'teiku' (let it stand unresolved).
items.desc: רבא מעלה סדרת ספקות לגבי קידושין בחצי פרוטה, בפרוטה אחת, ובחלוקה לזמנים. כל הספקות נותרו ללא פתרון (תיקו).

sub.desc_en: Rava asks whether saying 'half of you with a half-prutah, and half of you with a half-prutah' constitutes a fixed amount or ongoing counting.
sub.desc: רבא שואל על קידושין בחצי פרוטה פעמיים: האם כל אמירה נפרדת או שמא מצטרפות לפרוטה אחת.

sub.desc_en: Assuming ongoing counting, Rava asks whether saying 'half of you with a prutah and half of you with a prutah' fixes the matter or continues counting all day.
sub.desc: רבא שואל לגבי קידושין בפרוטה פעמיים באותו יום: האם נחשב כשתי פעולות נפרדות או שמא הכל מצטרף.

sub.desc_en: Assuming all-day counting, Rava asks whether saying 'half of you with a prutah today and half with a prutah tomorrow' fixes the matter or means betrothal begins now and completes tomorrow.
sub.desc: רבא שואל על קידושין בפרוטה היום ופרוטה למחר: האם נחשב כשתי פעולות נפרדות או שמא הקידושין מתחילים עכשיו ונגמרים למחר.

sub.desc_en: Rava asks whether saying 'two halves of you with a prutah' is valid or whether a woman cannot be betrothed in halves at all, concluding with 'teiku' (let it stand unresolved).
sub.desc: רבא שואל על קידושין בשני חצאין בפרוטה אחת: האם זה נחשב כדיבור אחד או שאין אשה מתקדשת לחצאין כלל, והבעיה נותרת בתיקו.

items.text: ספק רבא בשתי בנות בשתי פרוטות
items.text_en: Rava's question on betrothal of two daughters to two sons
items.desc_en: Rava asks whether in a case of betrothing two daughters to two sons with a single prutah, we follow the giver and receiver (where money exists) or the daughters and sons (where there is no money for each). The question remains unresolved (teiku).
items.desc: רבא שואל אם קידושין של שתי בנות בשתי פרוטות נחשבים כסך כולל או כסך נפרד לכל אחת. הספק נותר ללא פתרון.

sub.desc_en: Rava asks: if a man says 'your two daughters to my two sons with a peruta,' do we follow the giver and receiver (so there is monetary value), or the daughters and sons (so there is none)? The question stands unresolved (תיקו).
sub.desc: רבא שואל אם בקידושי שתי בנות בשתי פרוטות הולכים אחר הנותן והמקבל, ואז יש ממון, או אחר הבנות והבנים, ואז אין לכל אחד פרוטה; והספק נותר בתיקו.

items.text: ספק רב פפא בבת ופרה בפרוטה
items.text_en: Rav Pappa's question on betrothal with daughter and cow
items.desc_en: Rav Pappa asks whether betrothing 'your daughter and your cow with a prutah' means the daughter gets half a prutah and the cow half a prutah, or the daughter gets a full prutah and the cow is acquired by pulling. The question is left unresolved (teiku).
items.desc: רב פפא שואל אם קידושין של בת וקניית פרה בפרוטה אחת נחשבים כחלוקה או כסך כולל. הספק נותר ללא פתרון.

sub.desc_en: Rav Pappa asks: if a man says 'your daughter and your cow with a peruta,' do we allocate half a peruta to each, or the full peruta to the daughter and acquisition by pulling for the cow? The question stands unresolved (תיקו).
sub.desc: רב פפא שואל אם קידושי הבת וקניית הפרה בפרוטה אחת נחשבים כחלוקה או כסך כולל, והספק נותר ללא פתרון.

items.text: ספק רב אשי בבת וקרקע בפרוטה
items.text_en: Rav Ashi's question on betrothal with daughter and land
items.desc_en: Rav Ashi asks whether betrothing 'your daughter and your land with a prutah' means the daughter gets half a prutah and the land half a prutah, or the daughter gets a full prutah and the land is acquired by hazakah (possession). The question is left unresolved (teiku).
items.desc: רב אשי שואל אם קידושין של בת וקניית קרקע בפרוטה אחת נחשבים כחלוקה או כסך כולל. הספק נותר ללא פתרון.

sub.desc_en: Rav Ashi asks: if a man says 'your daughter and your land with a peruta,' do we allocate half a peruta to each, or the full peruta to the daughter and acquisition by hazakah (presumptive possession) for the land? The question stands unresolved (תיקו).
sub.desc: רב אשי מעלה ספק: אם אמר 'בתך וקרקעך בפרוטה', האם הכוונה לחלק את הפרוטה בין הקידושין לקניית הקרקע, או שהקרקע נקנית בחזקה והפרוטה כולה לקידושין? הספק נותר בתיקו.

items.text: מחלוקת רבה ורב יוסף בקידושין בשיראים
items.text_en: Dispute between Rabbah and Rav Yosef on appraisal of betrothal items
items.desc_en: A man betrothed with silk remnants. Rabbah says no appraisal is needed, Rav Yosef says it is needed. They agree that if he said 'with anything' no appraisal is needed, and if he said 'fifty' but they are not worth fifty, it is invalid. Their dispute is when he said 'fifty' and they are worth fifty: Rabbah says no appraisal needed since they are worth fifty, Rav Yosef says appraisal is needed because the woman is not expert in appraisal and does not rely on it. An alternative version holds they even dispute the case of 'with anything'.
items.desc: הגמרא מביאה מקרה של קידושין במשי, ויש מחלוקת בין רבה לרב יוסף אם צריך שומא. במקרה שאמר 'בכל דהו' כולם מודים שאין צריך, ובמקרה שאמר 'חמישין' ולא שווין כולם מודים שצריך. המחלוקת היא כשאמר 'חמישין' ושווין, ויש גם גרסה שנחלקו גם ב'בכל דהו'.

sub.desc_en: The gemara presents a case of a man who betrothed with silk remnants, and the dispute between Rabbah and Rav Yosef on whether appraisal is needed.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה מקרה של קידושין במשי, ומציגה את מחלוקת רבה ורב יוסף אם צריך שומא.

sub.desc_en: The gemara clarifies that if he said 'with anything', all agree no appraisal is needed.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שבמקרה שאמר 'חמישין' ולא שווין כולי עלמא מודים שצריך שומא.

sub.desc_en: The gemara clarifies that if he said 'fifty' but they are not worth fifty, all agree it is invalid.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שבמקרה שאמר 'חמישין' ולא שווין כולי עלמא מודים שצריך שומא.

sub.desc_en: The gemara identifies the disputed case: when he said 'fifty' and they are worth fifty.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שבמקרה שאמר 'חמישין' ולא שווין כולי עלמא מודים שצריך שומא.

sub.desc_en: Rabbah says no appraisal is needed because they are worth fifty.
sub.desc: הגמרא מביאה מקרה של קידושין במשי, ומציגה את מחלוקת רבה ורב יוסף אם צריך שומא.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef says appraisal is needed because the woman is not expert in appraisal and does not rely on it.
sub.desc: הגמרא מבהירה שבמקרה שאמר 'חמישין' ולא שווין כולי עלמא מודים שצריך שומא.

sub.desc_en: An alternative version holds that they even dispute the case of 'with anything'.
sub.desc: יש גרסה אחרת שנחלקו גם במקרה של 'בכל דהו', ורב יוסף מביא טעם: שווה כסף הרי הוא ככסף.

sub.text_en: Rav Yosef's reasoning in alternative version
sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef argues that an item equivalent to money is like money, just as money is fixed in value.
sub.desc: יש גרסה אחרת שנחלקו גם במקרה של 'בכל דהו', ורב יוסף מביא טעם: שווה כסף הרי הוא ככסף.

items.text: Opening statement: even items of uncertain value
items.text_en: Opening statement: even items of uncertain value
items.desc_en: The Gemara states that even items whose value is not fixed (דְּקִיץ) are considered equivalent to money for acquisition.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara opens by stating that even items of uncertain value (דְּקִיץ) are considered equivalent to money for acquisition.

items.text: Rav Yosef's proof from the baraita on acquisition
items.text_en: Rav Yosef's proof from the baraita on acquisition
items.desc_en: Rav Yosef cites a baraita that a field is acquired only with silver, not produce or vessels. The Gemara analyzes whether the baraita refers to items lacking a perutah's worth or items of uncertain value, concluding that it teaches that only fixed-value items work.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef opens by citing a baraita that a field is acquired only with silver (כֶסֶף), not with produce or vessels (תְּבוּאָה וְכֵלִים).

The Gemara asks: what is the case of produce and vessels? If they are worthless, the verse 'יָשִׁיב גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' (he shall return his redemption) already includes items of equivalent value (שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף) like silver.
The Gemara answers: the baraita refers to items that have a perutah's worth but lack a fixed value (לָא קַיְיצִי), so they cannot effect acquisition.

An alternative explanation: the baraita means that a field is acquired only through the mechanism of silver (תּוֹרַת כֶּסֶף), not through the mechanism of produce and vessels, which are actually חֲלִיפִין (exchange items).

items.text: Rav Nachman's objection and resolution
items.text_en: Rav Nachman's objection and resolution
items.desc_en: Rav Nachman holds that produce cannot effect exchange (חליפין), so the Gemara reinterprets the baraita as referring to items lacking a perutah's worth, teaching that even produce, whose benefit is immediate, does not work.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks: according to Rav Nachman, who holds that produce cannot effect exchange (חליפין), what can be said about the baraita?
The Gemara answers: the baraita actually deals with items lacking a perutah's worth, and it teaches that even produce, whose benefit is immediate, does not work.

The Gemara clarifies the baraita's teaching: it is not necessary to mention money, but produce and vessels, whose benefit is immediate, might be thought to work, so the baraita teaches that they do not.

items.text: Rav Yosef's second proof from redemption of the firstborn
items.text_en: Rav Yosef's second proof from redemption of the firstborn
items.desc_en: Rav Yosef cites a baraita about redeeming a son with an animal or garment worth five sela'im. The Gemara questions whether the item must be of fixed value, and concludes that the case is where the priest accepted the item despite its lower value, as with Rav Kahana.

sub.desc_en: Rav Yosef cites a baraita: if one says 'this calf for my son's redemption' or 'this cloak for my son's redemption' without specifying value, the son is not redeemed; but if he says 'this calf worth five sela'im for my son's redemption' or 'this cloak worth five sela'im for my son's redemption', the son is redeemed.

The Gemara asks: what are the circumstances of this redemption? If the item is not worth five sela'im, how can the father's declaration make it valid?
